title: M2A3 Bradley
name: m2a3_bradley
lede: The US Army's M2A3 Bradley infantry fighting vehicle at 1:1 scale, outside only: the two-man turret with its 25 mm M242 Bushmaster, coaxial M240C and twin TOW launcher, IBAS and the commander's independent viewer, add-on armour and skirts, the rear ramp for seven infantry, and the T157 track on six road wheels a side.
grid: Rear three-quarter view with the ramp lowered
The turret with the TOW launcher raised
Road wheels, skirts and the T157 track
game_note: Textured, with the turret, gun, TOW launcher, ramp, hatches, every wheel and each track link its own node.
viewer_note: orbit round it, drive it with the tracks running, traverse the turret, elevate the gun, raise the TOW launcher, lower the ramp and open the hatches.
scale_intro: Built to the published M2A3 figures; `build.py` measures the finished geometry against them on every build:
origin: on the ground, on the centreline, midway between the first and last road wheels
moving: traverses about local Y; + turns it left, all the way round
the 25 mm M242 and coaxial M240C: elevate about (−1, 0, 0); + raises them, −10° to +60°; over the hull roof and the squad's hatch its `limits_by_traverse` lift it to −6°
raises about local X at its back to the firing position (group `TOW launcher`)
lowers about local X at its foot, down to the ground (group `Ramp`); `Ramp_Door` opens in it (group `Ramp door`)
open about their hinges (group `Hatches`); the commander's stands open in front of the CIV
the commander's independent viewer slews about local Y on its own (`control: aux`)
spin about local X; each node's `radius` turns distance driven into rotation
the T157 track: one link mesh shared by every link node
head, blackout and tail lights; their lens materials `Light_White`, `Light_Amber` and `Light_Red` are emissive, so scale the emission to switch them
track_note: **Tracks.** Each `Track_*` node's extras carry the loop its links ride round (`path`: z and y pairs in the node's own frame, clockwise seen from the left), the link `pitch` and the number of `links`. Link *i* sits on the chord between the pins at *i*·pitch + travel and (*i* + 1)·pitch + travel, where travel is how far the vehicle has driven forward. That is all a game needs to run the tracks; the shared viewer does exactly this.
look: **Paint:** CARC green 383 with the add-on armour's seams and bolt rows and non-skid on the roof. Rebuild with `--scheme tan` for desert tan.
**Markings:** bumper codes (2-7IN, B-23), the vehicle number on the hull and the TOW launcher, the ramp's warnings.
**Weathering:** mud over the skirts and running gear, dust settled on top, exhaust soot streaming back from the outlet on the right, worn edges.
**Kit:** a rolled camouflage net and a duffel bag in the turret's bustle rack.
textures: Road wheels, idler, sprocket, rollers, suspension arms, the track link
accuracy: **Published dimensions:** length, width over the add-on armour, height to the top of the CIV, ground clearance, track width and the track's ground contact all match.
**Estimated:** the track centres, the idler and sprocket positions, the turret's plan, and the armour panels' layout.
